verifications.claim: TSA employees worked without pay for 44 days during a partial government shutdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'shutdown, which is entering its 45th day'; R3: '45-day partial government shutdown... began in mid-February'; R4: '44-day shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS)'; R5: 'After 44 days of working without pay'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm TSA worked without pay for approximately 44-45 days during partial DHS shutdown starting mid-February.

verifications.claim: Many TSA employees received retroactive paychecks on March 30, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Most of the Transportation Security Administration’s 60,000 workers began receiving back pay on Monday [March 30, 2026]'; R3: 'most TSA employees received a retroactive paycheck'; R4: 'Most TSA officers began getting paid Monday'; R5: 'most TSA employees received a first retroactive paycheck today [March 30]'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state most/many TSA employees received retroactive paychecks on March 30, 2026.

verifications.claim: Most TSA employees received retroactive paychecks covering their missed, unpaid work hours since the funding lapse began on Feb. 14, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'back pay that covered two full paychecks... since the partial government shutdown began... Feb. 14'; R3: 'retroactive paycheck featuring “at least two full paychecks” covering missed pay periods during the DHS shutdown that began Feb. 14'; R4: 'retroactive paychecks Monday for the weeks they have worked without pay during the partial... shutdown... started Feb. 14'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm most received pay covering missed hours since Feb. 14 lapse, though some note partial (e.g., half period pending), but claim aligns directly.

verifications.claim: President Trump issued an executive order requiring the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to pay TSA officers directly.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Trump signed an emergency directive ordering payment to TSA workers'; R2: 'memo that President Trump signed on Friday ordering the Department of Homeland Security to pay T.S.A. officers'; R3: 'Trump directed DHS to pay TSA officers'; R4: 'President Trump’s executive order... to pay TSA officers'; R5: 'President Trump issued an executive order... to pay TSA officers immediately'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Trump issued order/directive/memo requiring DHS to pay TSA officers using alternative funds.

verifications.claim: President Trump's executive order aims to alleviate staffing shortages caused by workers taking sick leave due to financial strain.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'operations are starting to return to normal after... ordering payment... TSA agents called out in record numbers'; R3: 'pay TSA officers... airport screening delays piled up'; R4: 'aimed at easing hours-long security wait times and encouraging... to show up to work, as callout rates topped 12 percent'; R5: 'some are still calling out sick... after weeks without income'
verifications.reasoning: Sources link EO to reducing high callout rates (sick leave) and lines/shortages from no-pay financial strain.

verifications.claim: Thousands of other DHS employees continue to work without pay.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'thousands more civilian employees across DHS will continue working unpaid'; R4: 'leaving many DHS employees without pay before the holiday break... fellow DHS employees are still not being paid'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state other DHS employees (thousands) continue unpaid while TSA gets paid.

verifications.claim: Some TSA employees reported the initial paychecks did not cover the entire period missed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'workers were still owed another week’s pay'; R3: 'process the half paycheck that TSA employees missed out on from the first week'; R4: 'might see some delays in receiving full back pay... several officers “have received incorrect pay amounts due to missing overtime payments'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm initial paychecks partial, missing some periods/overtime for some employees.

verifications.claim: Al Jazeera reported long security lines caused by high call-out rates during the shutdown
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 [Al Jazeera]: 'Following weeks of long lines at United States airport security checkpoints... TSA agents called out in record numbers over the weekend, with 10.59 percent calling out on Saturday and 12.35 percent on Friday'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (Al Jazeera) directly reports weeks of long lines with high callout rates during shutdown.
